page: Microsoft Azure DC4as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor featuring 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs with symmetric multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set capabilities include standard AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

System memory is configured at 16.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local disk storage, requiring network-attached remote block storage for operational file systems, though it supports Premium Storage configurations. No discrete GPU acceleration is included, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned by default.

Benchmark evaluations show moderate single-threaded capability alongside constrained multi-threaded scaling due to the 2-core underlying hardware. The server delivers average tier results in stress-ng single-core (1990.57) and Geekbench single-core (1224.0) tests, as well as Geekbench text processing (1569.0). In contrast, multi-core throughput falls into the lower quartile across tests such as Geekbench multi-core (2718.0), PassMark CPU (4766.46), software compilation with Clang (3359.0), and stress-ng multi-core (3963.09). Memory-bound tasks also measure in lower percentiles, with a PassMark memory score of 1733.45 and Redis SET throughput recording 3.43 million operations per second.

Given its balanced core-to-memory density and moderate compute performance, the DC4as_v5 provides a practical cost profile for light enterprise workloads. The lack of onboard storage requires factoring in external storage requirements. This virtual machine is best suited for general-purpose application servers, low-to-medium traffic web hosting, lightweight microservices, and development or continuous integration build agents with modest concurrency demands.
description: Microsoft Azure DC4as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The platform includes 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory allocation, but contains no local storage or GPU hardware. Performance metrics demonstrate middle-tier single-core CPU throughput, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 1224.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 1990.57. Multi-core performance is limited by the physical core count, placing the instance in the lower quartile for parallel tasks such as Clang compilation, ray tracing, and PassMark database operations. With Redis achieving 3.43 million SET operations per second, this instance is suited for lightweight enterprise services, low-load web servers, microservices, and staging environments that rely on external block storage.
